briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and xAI Grok-3 push frontier capabilities amid escalating compute race

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has intensified with multiple frontier labs releasing advanced reasoning models in the past month. Funding remains robust while regulatory scrutiny grows over deployment risks. Prompt injection and multi-agent security are emerging as critical bottlenecks for production systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with enhanced chain-of-thought capabilities while xAI released Grok-3 showing gains in real-time tool use. Anthropic's Claude 4 preview and Meta's Llama 4 405B variant continue the open-weight push. DeepSeek V3 and Google Gemini 2.5 Ultra also dropped this week.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New red-teaming reports highlight multi-agent coordination failures. EU AI Act enforcement begins targeting high-risk deployments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft and Google announced new 100k H100 clusters while TSMC reports record AI chip demand. xAI's Memphis supercluster expansion reached 300k GPUs. Energy constraints are delaying several planned builds into 2027.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent security protocols like dynamic dialect negotiation become mandatory for frontier deployments by 2027?
